entities.summary:
**Identity & Significance**: Didier of Cahors (didier-of-cahors), a Merovingian-era Merovingian royal official of aristocratic Gallo-Roman extraction, played a pivotal role in the 7th-century politics of the Frankish Kingdom (frankish-kingdom). Born around 610 and died on November 18, 655, he was instrumental in the governance of the kingdom.

**What Happened**: Didier of Cahors served as a royal official under King Chlothar III (chlothar-iii), expanding the kingdom's borders through strategic alliances and military campaigns. He also played a key role in the royal court's administrative reforms, streamlining the governance of the Frankish Kingdom.

**Legacy & Consequence**: Didier's administrative reforms had a lasting impact on the governance of the Frankish Kingdom, paving the way for the development of a more centralized and efficient state. His legacy can be seen in the subsequent reforms implemented by his successors.

**A Lasting Impact on the Franks**: Didier of Cahors' reforms led to the establishment of a more robust and effective administrative system, one that would shape the future of the Frankish Kingdom.
